materials.blurb: Olivine cathode: modest voltage, outstanding safety and cycle life, no cobalt or nickel.
The original commercial Li-ion cathode; cobalt-heavy.

properties.note: about half the Li is cycled

materials.blurb: High-nickel layered oxide: high capacity, less cobalt, harder to stabilise.
Nickel-cobalt-aluminium layered oxide used in long-range EV cells.
Manganese spinel: cheap and fast, but capacity fades at elevated temperature.
High-voltage cobalt-free spinel; needs electrolytes that survive ~4.7 V.
Higher-voltage cousin of LFP, held back by poor electronic conductivity.
NASICON-type sodium cathode with a flat 3.4 V plateau.
P2-type layered sodium oxide, nickel-manganese, cobalt-free.
Zero-strain titanate anode: very long life, low energy (high voltage vs Li).
The workhorse anode, intercalating Li to LiC6.
Alloying anode with ~10x graphite's capacity and ~300% volume swing.
Garnet oxide electrolyte, stable against Li metal. Conductivity depends dramatically on phase.
Sulfide superionic conductor rivalling liquid electrolytes; germanium is costly.
Glass-ceramic thiophosphate with liquid-like conductivity, moisture sensitive.
Halide-substituted argyrodite: the most widely studied sulfide electrolyte today.
Nanoporous β-Li3PS4, a classic sulfide baseline.
Chloride electrolyte with good oxidation stability for high-voltage cathodes.
Water-processable chloride electrolyte; indium is a scarce element.
Air-stable NASICON oxide; Ti4+ is reduced by lithium metal.
Amorphous thin-film electrolyte behind commercial micro-batteries.
The original NASICON sodium superionic conductor.
High-permittivity cyclic carbonate; forms the graphite SEI. Solid at room temperature.
Liquid cyclic carbonate; exfoliates graphite without additives.
Low-viscosity linear carbonate co-solvent.
Asymmetric linear carbonate, wider liquid range than DMC.
Ether solvent favoured for lithium-metal and Li-S cells.
Fluorinated additive that builds a LiF-rich SEI, key for silicon anodes.
Classic SEI-forming additive that polymerises on graphite.
The standard Li-ion salt: balanced properties, hydrolyses to HF.
Thermally stable imide salt; corrodes aluminium above ~3.8 V.
Imide salt with high conductivity, popular in high-concentration electrolytes.
Polymer host for solid polymer electrolytes; conducts well only above its melting point.
